action: Fugaku and Rikyu users: treat SSH and access keys used with these systems as exposed, replace them everywhere else they are used, check your own machines for unexpected logins and follow RIKEN's notices. Others: no action needed; for awareness.
date_note: Intrusion ran November 10-13 and Fugaku was shut down November 14; date is RIKEN's public notice of November 16.
exec: A national research supercomputer is offline with no restart date, and up to 4,597 users' access keys may have been exposed.
impact: Fugaku has been shut down since November 14 and users' login keys were disabled.
plain: Japan's flagship Fugaku supercomputer has been switched off since November 14 after an intruder got into its systems; data and login keys of up to 4,597 researchers may have been taken.
summary: RIKEN says an intruder reached Fugaku's internal servers between November 10 and 13 and installed malware; ITdaily and eSecurity Planet say the route was a public status page, which RIKEN is still investigating. Data of up to 4,222 Fugaku and 375 Rikyu users (up to 4,597) may have been taken, including SSH keys. Fugaku is offline with no restart date; no attacker is named.
title: Japan's RIKEN takes Fugaku supercomputer offline after intrusion

validation.note: BleepingComputer and The Register both report RIKEN's own statement; the RIKEN notice itself was not retrieved. The Register adds that someone attempted to log in to Fugaku on November 13 and that the attacker tried to use stolen credentials on other systems.

review.note: Compared against BleepingComputer (Nov 17) and The Register (Nov 17): intrusion Nov 10-13, shutdown Nov 14, 4,222 Fugaku + 375 Rikyu users (=4,597), SSH/access keys, dashboard entry, no attribution, no restart date all match.
